_why: A request document for `serverosctl ability resolve`, and deliberately a
MINIMAL one. The resolver consults eight inputs; this file names none of
them. It supplies the three SCALARS a request requires — an ability
reference, a device and a runtime — and the CLI turns only the first of
those into an input, and only when it is handed a catalogue to read
(`--ability-repo`/`--ability-rev`, or `--catalogue`). Without one the answer
is `inputs_seen: []` with all eight missing, which is the honest reading of a
request that names no catalogue; with one it reports `ability` as seen and
leaves seven missing. This file said "supplies three and names none of the
other five" until 2026-09-27, and the arithmetic was never checked against
the kernel's own output: the scalars are not among the eight, so the count
of the eight this file supplies is zero.
That is the point. `abilities/resolver.py` records which of the eight it
could read (`inputs_seen`) and which it could not (`inputs_missing`),
because a confident AVAILABLE computed from whichever inputs happened to be
readable is the failure the kernel exists to prevent. A request that filled
in all eight would demonstrate the resolver agreeing with its own caller;
this one demonstrates it saying what it could not see.
Until now the resolver had no example request anywhere in the tree, so the
only callers were its own tests. §45's question — can THIS device do THIS
thing, now, and if not why not — could not be asked from the CLI by anybody
who had not first read resolver.py.
`ability` is written as a REFERENCE (`ability:<id>`), which is what every
caller and every fixture in the product writes. It was written here as a
bare id, and that one spelling made this file demonstrate the opposite of
what it claims: the catalogue is keyed by reference, so the lookup missed
whatever catalogue the caller supplied, and the answer said `RUNTIME-
MANAGEMENT is not in the pinned catalogue` — a definite finding about a
catalogue that contains it. See `capability-contract.yaml#inputs[0]`,
where the key shape is now declared.
